To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

VSM-specific SirT1 deficiency increases arterial stiffness in the diet-induced model of metabolic syndrome and that VSM SirT-1 activation decreases arterial stiffening in the context of metabolic syndrome by inhibiting NF&kgr; B and p47phx expression and VCAM-1 protein expression.

(i) Vascular smooth muscle Sirtuin- (SirT)-1 protects against diet-induced aortic stiffness, (ii) SirT1 activation by resveratrol, S17834 or SRT1720 prevents arterial stiffness, and (iii) these beneficial effects are associated with a decrease of NF&kgr; B activation and VCAM-1 and p47phx protein expressions, in the aorta and Vascular Smooth Muscle (VSM) Cells.
vascular smooth muscle sirtuin-1 protects against diet-induced arterial stiffness in the mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel therapeutic target for preventing the development of arterial stiffness in obesity and metabolic syndrome.
the role of sirtuin-1, a deacetylase enzyme regulated by cellular energy metabolism, on arterial stiffness, a major risk factor of cardiovascular diseases.
the role of sirtuins in the development of atherosclerosis, the most common cause of death and disability in the Western world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

VSM SirT 1 activation decreases arterial stiffening in the setting of diet-induced obesity by stimulating anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory pathways in the aortic wall, and that pharmacological SirT1 activation may represent a novel approach to prevent arterial stiffening in overweight/obesity individuals with metabolic syndrome.
VSM-specific SirT1 over-expression prevents arterial stiffness in mice fed a HFHS diet for 8 months, by stimulating anti-inflammatory/antioxidant pathways in the aortic wall.
VSM SirT2 activation decreases arterial stiffness and associated vascular inflammation, in the setting of metabolic syndrome, by stimulating antioxidant pathways in the vascular wall.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VSM SirT 1 activation decreases arterial stiffnes in the setting of diet-induced metabolic disease, through anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects in VSM cells.
VSM SirT 1 protects against arterial stiffness in obesity by stimulating antiinflammatory and antioxidant pathways.
SirT1 activaion is a promising strategy to prevent arterial stiffness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VSM SirT 1 is an important regulator of arterial stiffness in the obese setting.
VSM Sirtuin- 1 (SIRT1) activation decreases arterial stiffness, a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, in the context of metabolic syndrome.
SirT1 activation in vascular smooth muscle prevents the development of arterial stiffness, a major risk factor for heart attack and stroke, in the setting of metabolic syndrome.
